notes: Both evaluate sgRNA 3' extension enhancement (C6, C25). LLM finds insufficient quantitative detail to fully evaluate the claim, while peer reviewers accept the improvement as demonstrated and note 'they improve on the guide RNA' as an advance.

Both assess efficiency quantification (C28, C29, C30). LLM finds the data UNSUPPORTED due to lack of statistical rigor, error bars, and replicates. Peer reviewers accept the efficiency data as SUPPORTED, acknowledging the reported range and comparison to ZFNs/TALENs without critique.

Both agree that lysate experiments (C5, C20, C23, C24, C31) successfully demonstrate sgRNA expression/assembly as the limiting factor. High claim overlap (83.3%) with consistent positive assessment of the mechanistic findings.

Both support the overall conclusion that RNA-programmed genome editing is feasible in human cells (C7, C27, C64, C66, C67). Peer reviewers describe it as 'excellent paper' demonstrating the capability, aligning with LLM's assessment of well-supported proof-of-concept.

Both address sequencing confirmation (C55). LLM finds it SUPPORTED as part of mutation confirmation evidence. Peer reviewers mark UNCERTAIN, requesting additional sequencing of cloned PCR products to demonstrate expected NHEJ mutation types, indicating current data is insufficient.

Both support Cas9 expression and nuclear localization (C17 shared). LLM evaluates broader construct design claims (C44, C45, C46, C68), while peer review focuses on overall demonstration. Agreement on the fundamental evidence of Cas9 functionality.
